about: Every mutant was applied to the file as it is at base_commit, which the change that adds this record does not change: it adds only tests, to the test module of the file's own tests (agent_import_span_identity_tests.rs). killer is the first test nextest reported failing (it stops at the first failure, with tests running in parallel, so another failing test may be reported first on another run). killer_at says where that test function exists: base, or this_commit for a test the change that adds this record adds. before_this_change gives the verdict at base where it differs. Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run, with no filter and nextest's --no-fail-fast, the approval stand-in example built) before it was called a survivor. One of the 101 hand-written mutants (S197) failed in that run, and its re-run failed again, each time in other tests that do not reach this file. The first time it failed in one approved_import test_seam dialog test (each_dialog_is_started_in_its_own_mode), which then passed 3 of 3 runs alone under S197 and 3 of 3 at base. The whole_set run was repeated for S197 once, took 3662 s (about 15 times the usual time, so the host was probably loaded or asleep), and failed three financial_mode_tests drain and mailing-read tests of tally::runtime (an_export_whose_mailing_answer_tally_declared_too_large_is_read_again_without_the_details, an_export_waits_out_the_drain_of_its_broken_off_mailing_read_before_reading_again and a_draining_refusal_after_part_of_the_standard_read_was_sent_is_not_waited_out). Those three were run together alone three times under S197 and three times at base: under S197 two runs passed and one failed (the last of the three, a timeout in a test double, in 40 s), at base one run failed all three (34 s each) and two passed. A test that fails at base is not a killer of this mutant. The whole_set run was then repeated once more for S197 (1046 s) and it survived all 5044 tests. Those failures were flakes, not kills: S197 counts as a survivor of the whole_set run, as the rest do, and the record credits no flaky test as a killer. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent, and one that is neither killed nor equivalent starts "not killed, and not equivalent:" and is counted under accepted_not_equivalent. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. Each edit's from text occurs exactly once in the file at base_commit, and applied_to names the file it was applied to. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. A mutant whose edit does not compile is recorded as unviable with the compiler's reason, not as caught. The survivors_again run was made against the 40 tests of the file's own test module (agent::agent_import::span_identity::tests::), the 24 that exist at base and the 16 this change adds, a subset of the tool and hand runs' filter in which every test this change adds lives and the only module whose tests the change alters; the other tests of the filter are as at base, so a mutant that survived the filter at base cannot be killed by them now. Every mutant that survived the whole_set run was run against all 40 of them after the last test was added, so a mutant killed there is killed by them, and every mutant that remains (each entry of accepted_survivors) was run against all of them. Every run was made on macOS with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1 and CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 (the object files and incremental cache of the target folder were cleared during the hand run to keep each build from slowing). The file has no platform-specific code (its only cfg is cfg(test) on the test module), so a macOS run measures every mutant in it on the code that Windows and Linux compile; the one width-dependent mutant, S107 (an as usize cast in place of usize::try_from), is recorded not killed, and not equivalent. No mutation run was made on Windows or Linux. The 16 tests this change adds carry no cfg attribute, so all of them run on macOS, Windows and Linux. S43's first edit was malformed and was rewritten: it called .map on the bool that the comparison yields, which does not compile (the compiler's reason was that `bool` is not an iterator), a defect of the edit and not a result for the mutant, so its edit was replaced by .then_some(CONCURRENT_CHANGE_LINE).or(Some(CONCURRENT_CHANGE_LINE)), the id was computed again from that edit, and the record holds only the rewritten mutant, which the tests of the filter catch. The hand-written mutants (S01 to S357) change, one at a time and by function (the count of mutants in brackets): PreMark::recorded (3); PreMark::value (3); SpanRefusal::code (28); concurrent_change_line_for (16); BindUnsettled::code (4); From<SpanRefusal> for BindError (2); clean_create (63); PostSpan::after_clean_response (15); PostSpan::after_clean_post (29); PostSpan::alter_id_span (9); bind (131); content_differences (53); PostedVoucherIdentity (1). Across the functions the edits include: dropping, negating and changing the operator of each condition; changing each match arm's code (to an empty string and to another arm's code); changing the order of the checks of clean_create, after_clean_post and bind; changing the arithmetic on the marks, the span and the MasterIDs (checked, wrapping, saturating and plain forms, one more and one less); moving a refusal to another position or another variant, or making it Unsettled; and dropping, renaming or reordering each field that content_differences compares. Not mutated: the derive lists, the items' visibility, the doc comments and other comments, the use line, the test module's attribute and path, the wording of CONCURRENT_CHANGE_LINE other than emptying it (one mutant); every edit above is one change (five mutants hold two edits), so none of the lists above is every possible change to the line it names. 84 edits (S08, S11, S13, S15, S19, S22, S25, S27, S35, S37, S44, S46, S49, S56, S57, S61, S64, S68, S72, S77, S81, S87, S96, S101, S103, S105, S109, S114, S117, S118, S129, S130, S133, S143, S150, S152, S153, S154, S155, S158, S160, S162, S170, S177, S183, S184, S199, S201, S205, S209, S212, S219, S225, S226, S229, S238, S239, S240, S243, S244, S248, S249, S252, S259, S279, S281, S286, S299, S300, S305, S308, S312, S314, S317, S322, S325, S329, S331, S333, S336, S342, S350, S352, S354) were respelled with one or more added spaces or by widening, because the first spelling gave a mutation id holding a run of eight or more decimal digits, which the privacy scan refuses. A respelling widens the from and the to text by the same whole tokens of context on either side; no space was added inside a string literal, a comment or an operator. Each respelled edit was checked with a lexer for Rust: the file after the edit has the same sequence of tokens (a string literal, a comment, an operator such as && or //, a name or a number each counting as one) as the file after the same edit written without the widening. Of the 357 hand-written mutants, none is unviable, 256 were caught at base and 101 survived the filtered run and the whole_set run; of those, this change's tests kill 77; 24 remain: 23 are equivalent and 1 is not killed and not equivalent (the reason of each is in accepted_survivors). Of the 60 mutants the tool found, 6 do not compile, 47 were caught at base and 7 survived (BindUnsettled::code with an empty string and with xyzzy, and the replacement of || by && at the first five of the seven || of clean_create); this change's tests kill all 7. In every run the file was byte for byte as at base_commit, checked after each restore (and, for the tool, after the run); the restore was a copy, never a rename. In the tool, hand and whole_set runs the test modules were as at base_commit; in survivors_again they are as this change leaves them.
